name: research
description: Research skills for reading the web well: fetch-web-sources reaches docs pages, code and repositories a plain fetch cannot see (llms.txt, markdown twins, token-less code / issue / repository search, open-source gates); watch-video extracts what a video says and shows (offline for local files, Gemini for YouTube, with a transcript knowledge file to chat from); link-rot-checker decides which of a batch of links are alive, dead or unknown, with a positive marker for each verdict.

interface.shortDescription: Read the web, code and video an agent's fetcher can't see
interface.longDescription: Research skills for the yystack marketplace. fetch-web-sources is a ladder of cheap, credential-free recipes for when a fetch comes back empty or 404: find the real docs path in llms.txt, ask for the markdown twin, search code and issues without a GitHub token, take an uptake census of a new product, and research an open-source deployment behind a login from its own public issues and docs. watch-video extracts content from a video — offline with ffmpeg and whisper.cpp for a local file, or through Gemini for YouTube, optionally saving a timestamped knowledge file to answer follow-ups from. link-rot-checker classifies a batch of links as alive, dead or unknown, demanding a positive marker for each verdict and a made-up-id control.
defaultPrompt: This docs page comes back empty — get me its content.
Find every public repository that contains this exact string.
Summarise this YouTube talk and extract the steps.
Which of these saved links still work?
